# Remotion 4.0.535 compatibility

Setup refuses an incompatible project and lists the complete required pins,
including the Remotion packages, React and React DOM. For an older
project, explicitly pin every listed dependency in `package.json`, review the
timing changes below, then rerun setup to install them and refresh the official
skills. No package-manager lockfile is required before setup: setup validates the
manifest, then runs npm install.

## Playback speed and loops

Since 4.0.530, `durationInFrames` selects the amount of child or media content
before `playbackRate` is applied. The visible duration in the parent timeline is
`durationInFrames / playbackRate`. This applies to sequences and audio/video
components; `trimBefore` advances the source start, and looping repeats the
selected range. The root composition's duration still sets the export length.

## WebM and constrained bitrate

For VP8, VP9 and AV1, setting `encodingBufferSize` also requires `videoBitrate`.
On the CLI, pair `--buffer-size` with `--video-bitrate`.

# Rights and delivery

For asset rights, credits, subtitles and delivery checks.

## Core

- Deliver a `CREDITS` file naming every third-party asset (samples, music, fonts, images, the voice engine) with its source and licence; credit on screen where a licence requires it; tell the user `CREDITS` lists the licences and the material is their responsibility.
- `voyager media review FILE` measures loudness but flags only a true peak above 0 dBTP (clipping): check `audio.integratedLUFS` near −14 and `audio.truePeakDBTP` at or below −1 yourself. It also checks black frames and duration. When the audio is a person's recording, review the processed voice stem (not the final mix with music) and pass the recording as `--audio-source`: review then flags a noise floor raised more than 15 dB or crushed dynamics; never force a very quiet recording to the target.
- To judge continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use a video-understanding model with `voyager models run`; load `choose-media-model/references/understanding.md` for the paid upload route.

--- name: remotion description: "." applications: - id: remotion role: primary voyager: schemaVersion: 1 design: optional craft: [rights-and-delivery] --- Create one project per piece inside the active workspace, named for the piece: ```sh voyager remotion setup .//motion --json ``` When the project has a selected brand kit (`brand/manifest.json`, with the kit in `brand/BRAND.md`), read it as [brand-kit](../brand-kit/SKILL.md) describes before designing any frame, and use its colours, fonts and logos. When the brand has captured motion (`brand/motion.json`), setup and every run write `src/brand-motion.ts`, generated from it (do not edit; change motion.json instead). Use it for every title, lower third, caption and card: spread `titleStyle(frame, fps, text)` into a wrapper around the text (it sets transform, opacity, filter and clip-path). For a brand whose titles punch in (`punchIn` is not null), `titleStyle` shows the words small for the title-in, then hard-cuts them to full size; to give the small words their own shot, split the title with `titleShots(frames, fps)` (`{from, durationInFrames, scale}` per Sequence) and set only that scale on the text, instead of `titleStyle`, never both. Size scenes with `shotFrames(totalFrames, fps)` and put `brandTransition(fps, totalFrames)` between them in a `TransitionSeries` (it is `null` for a brand that cuts: put no Transition there), so cuts land at the brand's pace; setup starts a new project cut this way. In an edit of real footage, use it only for titles, lower thirds, captions and cards: keep the footage's own rhythm, add no brand transitions to its cuts, and add no logo reveal or end card the brief did not ask for. When the brand has font files (`brand/assets/fonts/`, or a site kit's `fonts/`), setup and every run write `src/brand-fonts.ts` and copy the files to `public/brand-fonts/` (do not edit). Only when the setup or run result's `brandFonts.path` is present and `brandFonts.skipped` is not, add `import "./brand-fonts";` once in the root; otherwise do not import it (the file does not exist, or is the user's). Use the brand's family names in `fontFamily`; never hand-write `@font-face`. `brandFonts.notice` names any family that fell back; tell the user. Setup has no background mode, so give the command a shell timeout of at least 10 minutes. If setup is cut off anyway, run the same command again: it discards the half-finished install and reinstalls, reusing the packages it already downloaded. When parsing JSON, read stdout only; do not merge stderr with `2>&1`. Progress notices and live tool output go to stderr. Setup installs Remotion 4.0.535, matching packages, official skills and Chrome using Voyager's bundled runtime. Setup's JSON `skills` field is the absolute path of the official skill router (`.../remotion-best-practices/SKILL.md`); open that exact file and its relevant references. Its links are relative to that file's folder; there is no `rules/` folder. Use them for Remotion craft; where their preview, rendering or delivery workflow differs from Voyager's skills, follow Voyager's skills: previews and stills are progress checks, not stopping points, and a requested video is complete only when its full render, made with `voyager remotion run`, is presented as the deliverable. If their download failed, setup still succeeds with `skillsSkipped` and a warning instead of `skills`: work without them; the next setup retries. Read [version compatibility](references/compatibility.md) when upgrading a project, changing playback speed or exporting WebM. Remotion bundles for Chrome 85, which rejects top-level `await`: never use it in code Remotion bundles. Instead, call `loadFont(...)` at module scope without `await`, once per weight or style: it delays the render until the font is ready. Run the official CLI through Voyager: ```sh voyager remotion run .//motion -- ``` For a standalone HTML preview, use `export-html`. It embeds only the `public/` files the code names; if the composition builds file names at runtime or lists files with `getStaticFiles()` and the export warns that files were left out, rerun with `--all-public`. ## Cut footage in the composition Screen recordings and other source footage are cut, cropped, masked and held in the composition, never pre-cut with ffmpeg. Copy each source file once into `public/footage/` with `cp`, not a symlink (a linked file fails the render with a 404), and leave it whole. Of the official `ffmpeg.md` trimming options, use the preferred `trimBefore`; never its ffmpeg re-encode. The only ffmpeg step is a one-time transcode of a whole file the render cannot decode (Apple ProRes fails with `ProResDecoderNotEnabledError`): `ffmpeg -i take.mov -c:a aac public/footage/take.mp4`. The `ffmpeg` on your PATH has no `libx264`; take the video arguments for this OS from [bundled FFmpeg encoders](../make-social-loop/references/delivery.md#bundled-ffmpeg-encoders) (macOS `-c:v h264_videotoolbox -q:v 85`). H.264 or HEVC `.mov` and `.mp4` play as they are. - **Trim**: `trimBefore` skips source frames; the clip's `` `durationInFrames` ends it. - **Frame the recording**: put the video, filling it, in a wrapper sized in pixels to the recording's own shape, fitted to the composition from `useVideoConfig()` (by height below; by width when the recording is wider than the composition) and centred in an `overflow: hidden` box. A 16:10 Mac recording in a 16:9 composition is otherwise letterboxed inside the wrapper, and every percent below misses. - **Crop or zoom**: CSS `scale` and `transformOrigin` on that wrapper.
